ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.Self)` (Wish.cs:15-18) == cost 0 / SKILL / ANCIENT / SELF. No CanonicalVars -- exactly one card is taken.

OnPlay.rationale: `CardSelectCmd.FromCombatPile(prefs: (prompt, 1), pile: PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner))` with NO filter, then `CardPileCmd.Add(cardModel, PileType.Hand)` if non-null (Wish.cs:22-26) == `ctx.combat.select_cards('wish', list(player.draw_pile), 1)` then the manual draw-pile-to-hand move. The absence of a filter is right -- Wish takes ANY card from the draw pile, unlike card/secret_technique (Skills) and card/secret_weapon (Attacks) -- and Wish cannot pick itself on either side, since it is not in the draw pile. The sim calls `select_cards` directly rather than through `CardSelectCmd.from_pile`, which is the same call one layer down (cmds.py:1817-1832, moved from :532-542 -- content re-verified current, same `is_draw_pile`/`min_select` shape). BLAST RADIUS, not re-verdicted per rule 3: `CardSelectCmd` auto-selects with no player choice and no RNG at or below MinSelect (CardSelectCmd.cs:287-290) where the sim's `select_cards` (combat.py:1475-1545, moved from :575-581; re-verified current) always delegates and otherwise falls back to a uniform-random pick with the combat RNG -- creature_card_cmds steps 104/105.

OnUpgrade.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): STICKY KEYWORD FIXED AT THE SEAM, per binding rule 3 -- see creature_card_cmds/step52. `Card.downgrade` (cards/base.py) now deletes the instance-level shadow of every CardKeyword-backed attribute before re-running `_init_vars`, which is `DowngradeInternal`'s `_keywords = cardModel.GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local).ToHashSet()` (CardModel.cs:2143). The card file itself is UNCHANGED: the defect was never in `_on_upgrade`, which faithfully ports `AddKeyword`/`RemoveKeyword`, but in the rebuild that was supposed to undo it -- which is why a per-card `_init_vars` line would have been the wrong fix, needing to be repeated for every future card. `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` goes 5 of 203 -> **0 of 203**. Pinned by test/test_downgrade_rebuild.py::test_upgrade_then_downgrade_restores_the_keyword and by a pool-wide sweep over all seven keywords. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Retain)` (Wish.cs:31) maps to `self.retain = True`, correct at upgrade level 1. DOWNGRADE IS STICKY: `Card.downgrade` (cards/base.py:324-353, moved from the historical :150-165 citation) rebuilds by re-running `_init_vars` and re-applying upgrades, and `WishCard._init_vars` (wish.py:24-25) sets only `_energy_cost` -- it never re-seeds `retain` -- so the instance attribute written by `_on_upgrade` survives and a downgraded Wish is still Retained. C# `DowngradeInternal` rebuilds the whole keyword set from canonical (CardModel.cs:2143). EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` prints `wish: retain: False -> True` -- this is the FIFTH and LAST of the five sticky cards the probe found, completing the set with card/aggression, card/apparition, card/hello_world and card/juggling. LIVE: `downgrade()` is reachable from `events/reflections.py:40`, `events/welcome_to_wongos.py:90` (both registered in `events/__init__.py`) and `powers.py` (DampenPower, currently at powers.py:3968 -- moved from the historical :3171 citation, re-verified still downgrades every upgraded card in AllCards). Observable: a downgraded Wish is never discarded by the end-of-turn hand flush in the sim; in the game it is. The one-line fix is `self.retain = False` in `_init_vars`, exactly as card/scrawl and card/gold_axe -- which gain the same keyword on upgrade -- already do. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/aggression's OnUpgrade entry (rule 3).

guards.what: the sim returns early on an empty draw pile (wish.py:32-33) and does not check MAX_HAND_SIZE where card/secret_technique does
guards.rationale: The early return matches C#'s `FirstOrDefault()`-is-null skip. The missing hand-size check is harmless: C#'s `CardPileCmd.Add` enforces `CardPile.MaxCardsInHand` inside AddInternal, but Wish moves exactly one card and is itself leaving the hand as it resolves, so the hand can never be at 10 when the moved card arrives. Recorded because the sibling card DOES check, so the asymmetry is a checked fact rather than an oversight.
